record.paper_title: The Higgs program and open questions in particle physics and cosmology
record.context_brief: Flavor puzzles and Higgs Yukawa measurements
record.original_question: What is the solution to the flavor puzzles in particle physics: why the charged fermion masses and CKM mixing angles have small, hierarchical structure; why neutrino-related flavor parameters appear not to show comparable hierarchy, degeneracy, or smallness; and, if there is TeV-scale new physics, what alignment or degeneracy mechanism prevents it from producing large deviations in flavor-changing neutral current processes? Can measurements of Higgs Yukawa couplings and flavor-violating Higgs-related processes distinguish among proposed solutions?

evidence.quote:
Here is a list of seven open questions at the forefront of particle physics and cosmology, to which the Higgs program may provide answers:
7. What is the solution of the ﬂavor puzzle(s)?

IV. WHAT IS THE SOLUTION OF THE FLA VOR PUZZLE(S)?
There are several reasons that make the study of ﬂavor physics via Higgs physics well motivated. First, ﬂavor
physics raises three puzzles [ 30]:
• The Standard Model ﬂavor puzzle: Why is there structure (smallne ss and hierarchy) in the charged fermion
masses and the CKM mixing angles?
• The neutrino ﬂavor puzzle: Why, in contrast to the charged fermio ns, there seems to be no structure (neither
hierarchy nor degeneracy nor smallness) in the neutrino-related ﬂ avor parameters?
• The new physics ﬂavor puzzle: If there is new physics at the TeV sca le, what is the mechanism (alignment
and/or degeneracy) that prevents it from signiﬁcantly modifying t he SM predictions for ﬂavor changing neutral
current processes?

Various models have been suggested to answer one or more of thes e questions. The best hope to make further
progress is by measuring new ﬂavor parameters (beyond the matr ix elements of the CKM matrix). Measurements of
the Yukawa couplings of h provide such an opportunity.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In the Standard Model of particle physics, the Yukawa interactions between the Higgs doublet and the three generations of quarks and charged leptons give rise, after electroweak symmetry breaking, to the charged fermion mass matrices, whose diagonalization yields the observed mass eigenvalues and the Cabibbo–Kobayashi–Maskawa (CKM) mixing matrix V_CKM in the quark sector. The neutrino sector is described analogously by the (Majorana or Dirac) neutrino mass matrix and the Pontecorvo–Maki–Nakagawa–Sakata (PMNS) mixing matrix. Empirically:

(a) The charged fermion masses span many orders of magnitude (m_e ≪ m_μ ≪ m_τ, m_u ≪ m_c ≪ m_t, m_d ≪ m_s ≪ m_b) and the CKM mixing angles are small and hierarchical.
(b) The neutrino mass-squared splittings Δm²_{21} and |Δm²_{31}| are within two orders of magnitude of each other, and the PMNS mixing angles are all O(1) (with the exception of θ_13, which is small but not very small).
(c) Generic new physics at the TeV scale, coupling to Standard Model fermions with O(1) flavor-arbitrary couplings, would induce flavor-changing neutral current (FCNC) processes (e.g., K⁰–K̄⁰ mixing, B⁰_{(s)}–B̄⁰_{(s)} mixing, μ → eγ, μ → e conversion) at rates orders of magnitude above current experimental bounds.

Provide a theoretical framework that simultaneously:

(i) Explains the smallness and hierarchical pattern of the charged fermion masses and CKM mixing angles.
(ii) Explains why the neutrino mass and mixing parameters fail to exhibit a comparable hierarchy, degeneracy, or smallness pattern.
(iii) Specifies, assuming TeV-scale new physics, the alignment and/or degeneracy mechanism by which the new physics avoids generating FCNC contributions in conflict with experimental constraints.

In addition, identify a set of observables among the Yukawa couplings y_f of the 125 GeV Higgs boson h (in particular flavor-diagonal couplings to second-generation fermions, such as h → μ⁺μ⁻ and h → cc̄) and flavor-violating Higgs decays (such as h → τμ, h → τe, h → eμ) whose measured values would discriminate among competing frameworks satisfying (i)–(iii).

artifact.status_search_result: The flavor puzzle remains an outstanding open problem in particle physics. While numerous candidate frameworks (Froggatt–Nielsen U(1) flavor symmetries, non-abelian discrete flavor symmetries, partial compositeness/Randall–Sundrum, modular flavor symmetries, MFV ansätze, etc.) address parts of (i)–(iii), no consensus solution exists, and ongoing programs at the LHC and future colliders aim to measure h → μμ, h → cc and search for h → τμ to discriminate among them. Recent reviews (2023–2025) continue to list the flavor puzzle as unsolved.

status_evidence.title: Flavor physics and CP violation (review)
status_evidence.snippet: The Standard Model flavor puzzle and the new physics flavor puzzle remain among the central open questions; ongoing experimental program needed to discriminate models.
status_evidence.claim: Flavor puzzles still listed as open.

status_evidence.title: ATLAS/CMS measurements of H→μμ
status_evidence.snippet: First evidence for H→μμ has been reported, beginning the program of measuring second-generation Yukawa couplings.
status_evidence.claim: Higgs Yukawa measurements relevant to discriminating flavor models are in progress, not conclusive.
